newsitem.title: USA: Mexico drugs debate expected this week in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico drugs debate expected this week in Senate.

text.p: Senate Republican leader Trent Lott said on Monday he expected the Senate would debate this week a resolution on Mexican cooperation in the anti-drug war.

The House of Representatives last week voted to give Mexico 90 days to improve its performance or face "decertification" as a reliable ally in the fight against drugs. The Clinton administration strongly opposed the House measure, which is harshly critical of its own anti-drug policies.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin led a high-level delegation to Capitol Hill for a meeting with a bipartisan group of senators on Monday evening to discuss a possible compromise that would enable Congress to express its dissatisfaction with Mexico while not provoking a crisis that could harm relations between the two countries.
Senators participating in the meeting included Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, Sen. Kay Bailey Hutchison, a Texas Republican, and Sen. Paul Coverdell, a Georgia Republican.

"There's a bipartisan effort under way to see what can be agreed to that would make our feelings very clear that we are dissatisfied with the degree of cooperation and the results that we're getting from the so-called war on drugs," Lott said.
He added: "At the same time I think there is a feeling that we don't want to cut off the continuing law enforcement effort and communications ... that might worsen the situation."

Lott said he expected to bring up the issue on the Senate floor on Wednesday or Thursday. He said he assumed a Senate resolution would differ from the House version but would have to be stronger than an alternative proposed by Hutchison that would merely express congressional views on Mexico's anti-drug performance without the force of law.
